annotations.title: Find the eclipses near a date

description:
Finds the solar and lunar eclipses nearest a date: greatest eclipse to the second in UTC, type, obscuration, the eclipsed body's sign, days from the date, and for a solar eclipse where greatest eclipse meets the Earth. Given a place, each listing ALSO carries what that observer gets: local kind, first contact, maximum, last contact and altitude at each.

DELEGATE THIS RATHER THAN DERIVING IT: the 6,585.3-day saros puts eclipses in families easy to confuse by a year or a continent, and A GLOBAL ECLIPSE IS NOT AN EVENT FOR EVERYBODY. This keeps global and local circumstances apart, including the Moon setting partway through or rising with the eclipse underway.

CITATION: required. See server instructions.

count.description: How many per side of the date, "1" to "12", default "3". Example: "1". Ask for what you will use.

date.description: The date to search AROUND, ISO YYYY-MM-DD, 1700-2200. Example: "2026-08-12". Need not be an eclipse date.

family.description: Which eclipses to list: "both" (the default), "lunar" or "solar".

lat.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees as a string. Example: "64.1466". Send with lon.

lon.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees as a string. Example: "-21.9426". Send with lat.

place.description: Observer town or city. Example: "Reykjavik, Iceland". Adds the local kind, contact times and altitudes.

tz.description: IANA zone or numeric UTC offset hours for the local contact times. Example: "Atlantic/Reykjavik".

name: find_eclipses
title: Find the eclipses near a date
